status: PROPOSED code; semantics approved by the Board (KA-BD-5, approved with amendment, 2026-11-23)

evaluation: 1. scope does not match (entity tags, action category, representation) -> not_applicable, with the reason

2. scope cannot be decided (category missing or not in the vocabulary) or the quantity cannot be measured (invalid input, unsupported structure or representation, or a missing phase, event, joint mapping, range, facing, ground line or threshold) -> unknown with the reason and its unknown_kind. unknown is never pass
4. measured outside the threshold -> fail only when the rule is enforcement-eligible, otherwise warn
5. artistic review items -> unknown (awaiting review) until a valid review record exists
semantics.enforcement_eligibility: A rule may fail only when it is enforcement-eligible. structural_invariant rules are eligible by class (each states its rationale). Any other rule needs all of: enforcement.eligible true with a recorded rationale and approver, a measurement convention that matches the rule's quantity for the representation measured, a representation suited to the quantity, and (for anatomical values) value provenance marked gate_eligible. Verified source data alone does not make a rule eligible. A screen-projected 2D proxy compared with a 3D anatomical table is never eligible (warn at most).
semantics.acceptance: Any fail in a mandatory criterion -> rejected. Otherwise any unknown in a mandatory criterion -> blocked (names what is missing). warn and advisory unknown are reported and do not block. Every verdict lists the counts of all five states and the defect classes this rule set cannot detect.

classes.structural_invariant: hierarchy, connectivity, rigid object count and attachment, declared contacts, non-interpenetration of a rigid object with the static ground; eligible by class
classes.representation_constraint: a limitation or assumption of the representation (planar projection); warn at most
classes.anatomical_reference: anatomical ranges from the anatomy profile; warn unless every eligibility condition holds
classes.physical_approximation: simplified physics (x-only support, unverified mass table); warn at most
classes.action_specific: intent rules for one action category (heavy overhead strike benchmark); warn unless an enforcement record exists
classes.artistic_heuristic: coupling and continuity rules of thumb; warn at most
classes.artistic_review: human judgement on the previews; unknown until a review record exists, then the recorded decision
classes.declaration: the motion or structure declares something the rules need (category, representation, acceptance profile); pass or unknown only (meta.acceptance_overrides warns when a loosening request was refused)

semantics.ownership: Board code review of PR #110 (110-01): motion data, the approved validation (acceptance) profile, approved action-specific criteria, approved exceptions and the implementation are separate. Acceptance roles (mandatory/advisory) come only from the acceptance profile in this registry, and the thresholds of structural invariants only from the rule records here (threshold.owner 'registry'). A motion file can only tighten: promote a rule to mandatory in acceptance.roles, or set a stricter structural threshold. A request to demote a rule or loosen a structural threshold is refused, the registry value is used, and meta.acceptance_overrides reports the refusal (warn). A mandatory rule becomes advisory for one motion only through an entry of approved_exceptions (scope, provenance, approval record) that the motion references in acceptance.exceptions [{id, rule, why}]; a reference without a valid entry is refused and reported. Every acceptance profile must list every structural invariant and every always_mandatory declaration as mandatory (checked when the registry loads).
semantics.unknown_kinds: every unknown carries unknown_kind: invalid_input (an error result naming the field: malformed or out-of-range data, missing references, non-finite numbers), unsupported (valid data outside the declared supported_scope or representation), unmeasurable (valid, supported data whose quantity cannot be measured: a missing phase, event, threshold, facing, ground line, mapping or tier). Input is validated before the solver runs; there is no blanket exception handler, so a programming error still raises.
semantics.representation_scope: A structural invariant applies to every representation unless the rule states scope.representation_exclusion_why (checked when the registry loads). The representation is validated before solving: only a representation with a solver in vocabularies.representations is solved.

planar_2d.solver: motion.Solver (planar FK chains, two-bone leg IK, rigid attachments)
planar_2d.note: the only representation a solver here can measure; the measured representation is always the solver's, never the structure's self-declaration

depth_3d.note: no depth-aware solver exists; a structure that declares it gets meta.representation unknown (its numbers would be planar measurements labelled as 3D)

categories.strike.heavy_overhead: heavy overhead weapon strike (the benchmark action)
categories.pose.static: two-frame static clip built by poselib.py for one pose

vocabularies.note: closed vocabularies: an unrecognised representation or category is unknown (blocking where mandatory), never not_applicable. Add a category here before using it.

supported_scope.status: the solver (motion.Solver) is an R&D spike validated on ONE structure: data/structure_brute_hammer.json (heavy-hammer benchmark). It is not a universal entity solver (Board code review of PR #110, 110-04).
validated: planar_2d humanoid biped: chain 'trunk' (base root, joints pelvis then chest), arm chains based on trunk joints, two-bone legs hanging off 'pelvis' planted on contacts with toe/heel points, exactly one rigid attachment named 'hammer' whose object declares points head and butt, an anatomy profile extending humanoid_base
actions: strike.heavy_overhead (B, C), locomotion.idle and locomotion.walk on the same hammer humanoid (synthetic fixtures), pose.static (poselib)
unsupported: attachments with another name or more than one attachment (sword, shield, dual wield)
quadrupeds, multi-limbed and flying profiles (anatomy profile not extending humanoid_base)
hovering or flying entities (no legs or contacts)
depth_3d or any representation without a solver
supported_scope.result: a structure outside the validated scope gets meta.solver_scope unknown (unknown_kind unsupported), mandatory, so the verdict is blocked with the reason; the solver is not run, so no structural rule can pass or be not_applicable by accident

approved_exceptions_schema.effect: the rule is advisory for the scoped motions

review_binding: an artistic review record counts only when bound to the exact reviewed revision: motion_sha256, structure_sha256, validation_profile_sha256 (canonical JSON, posecheck.review_binding), artwork_sha256 when the artwork file is available, evidence files with sha256, reviewer and date. Any material change invalidates it (stale). A recorded visual review is not governed approval: the artistic items take the recorded decision only with a separate approval record (ref, approved_by different from the reviewer, role board or qa, date, review_sha256 of the review record); otherwise they stay unknown (awaiting governed approval).

default.note: role_in_acceptance per rule id. Unlisted rules are advisory: the heavy-strike action-specific, artistic-heuristic and biomechanics rules are advisory by default (Board code review of PR #110, 110-06); they become mandatory only through an approved action-specific acceptance profile, and none is approved yet. A motion selects a profile with acceptance.profile; an unknown profile, or one whose categories do not cover the motion's category, makes meta.acceptance_profile unknown and the default roles are used.

pose_library.note: used by poselib.py for static poses: the same mandatory set without the artistic review items (a pose is reviewed in the library sheet, not per clip). Replaces the motion-level roles entry poselib used before; only category pose.static may select it.

coverage_gaps: depth-order changes (arm or weapon passing behind or in front of the body): planar rig has no depth
3D self-intersection (limb or weapon path through the body or head); face_zone_overlap is a 2D screen-overlap proxy
foreshortening and visible-length changes: the planar rig keeps projected length constant by construction
hinge bend side and hyperextension on channels mapped with sign 'abs'
axial rotations (forearm pronation/supination, humeral rotation): not measurable as a 2D angle
shoulder flexion vs abduction (a side-view elevation angle cannot separate them)
environment penetration other than the ground line (walls, props, other characters)
transition continuity between clips, loop seams, draw-order stability
readability at game scale and appeal (only through the artistic review record)
impact silhouette change (computed only by motion.py save_all, not by this validator)

rules.statement: the motion file uses a schema this validator can solve (motion.v2)
the motion declares its action category (scope of action-specific rules) and the category is in vocabularies.categories
the structure declares a representation from vocabularies.representations, and it is the representation the solver measures
rules.note: rules are always scoped by the solver's (measured) representation; this rule makes a missing, misspelt or unsupported declaration visible and blocking

rules.statement: the motion's acceptance.profile (default 'default') is a profile of this registry whose categories cover the motion
structure and motion are well-formed before solving: references exist, frames, phases, events and constraint spans are in range, every number is finite (an invalid field is named)
the structure is inside the solver's declared supported_scope (otherwise unsupported: not solved, blocked)
the motion's acceptance block only tightens (promotes rules, stricter structural thresholds); a refused loosening request warns
every joint parent exists

enforcement.rationale: a skeleton whose parent is missing is not a hierarchy; nothing downstream is defined

rules.statement: no part of the rigid weapon goes below the floor line

threshold.status: experimental and benchmark-specific: 3.0 px of the heavy-hammer benchmark master canvas (brute_hammer, 832x1216 px, no game-scale conversion), a numerical tolerance for that one structure, not a universal Studio threshold; awaiting Board confirmation of the rule's justification and value
threshold.units: px of the structure's own canvas (scales with the art; another structure needs its own value)
threshold.exceptions: none approved; a motion may only make it stricter

refs: U1 comparison 2026-11-22 (B sinks the hammer below the floor for 34 frames)
source.justification: ported from the R&D copy via review (KA-BD-11)

enforcement.rationale: non-interpenetration of a rigid object with the static ground. In the planar rig's own model every bone and the attached object lie in one plane whose floor is the line the structure declares (ground.line_y, or its contact points: contacts.ground_y + toe/heel y), so screen y below that line is exact penetration in that model, not a projected proxy. The finding names the ground reference used. A motion that means the weapon to be nearer the camera than the body cannot express that on a planar rig and must use a depth-aware rig.

rules.statement: the anatomical angle stays inside the profile range for the structure's limit tier

enforcement.scope_note: profile tables are 3D normative references (means or textbook values), not ceilings; no Board enforcement record exists

rules.statement: a hinge bends to its anatomical side (no hyperextension past the tier's lower bound)
rules.note: channels mapped with sign 'abs' cannot measure bend side: unknown, never pass

rules.statement: every joint movement the anatomy profile declares is measured by some channel
rules.note: emits unknown for each unmapped profile movement so a missing check is visible

rules.statement: the arm does not go behind the trunk beyond the tier's extension bound (below 150 deg of 2D elevation)

rules.statement: the knee stays on the facing side of the hip-ankle line (2D)

rules.statement: the centre of mass x stays over the x-span of the contacts (+-4 px)

threshold.why: no source; mass table 'to be verified'

rules.statement: the COM moves back (against the facing) in the wind-up
the COM is forward (along the facing) at impact
the striking elbow is nearly straight at impact (2D interior angle)
the striking elbow is most bent at the top of the wind-up (last 8 frames)
the striking elbow uses enough range over the clip (v1 'elbow kept bent')
the weapon turns against the strike in the wind-up and with it in the swing (character frame)

threshold.literal: windup turn < 0 < swing turn (multiplied by facing)

rules.statement: the weapon overshoots the impact angle in the follow-through (character frame)
the weapon angle moves one way through the swing (character frame)
the weapon head is still fast at contact (no braking before contact)
peak speed frame does not decrease from pelvis to spine to elbow to weapon in the swing

refs: biomechanics §1.1: a strong tendency, not a law (throwing data)

rules.statement: an arm above about 120 deg of 2D elevation raises the shoulder joint (shift y < -2 px), at most 2 frames off

threshold.why: no source for these numbers (profile states ~2:1 above ~30 deg)

rules.statement: no single frame where the weapon head is much faster than both neighbours
intent reads at game scale (270 px)
phase poses read (anticipation, contact)
personality and weight of the character
natural vs intentionally stylised posture
comparison with the motion reference
